findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "check_booking_link" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Free, instant pre-flight check for a booking URL. Classifies which booking platform a URL belongs to and tells you whether import_booking_url will accept it, WI…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "mint_key" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Agent self-serve API key issuance. An autonomous agent that has no email inbox can obtain a free-tier API key by proving it holds the MACHINE_MINT_SECRET via HM…

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: handle_inbound, check_booking_link, check_compliance, screen_sanctions, get_conversation · Private data: verify_business, check_quota, verify_company_record, mint_key · Public sink: send_message, capture_lead, send_transactional_confirmation, check_compliance, mint_key · Destructive: check_compliance.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: handle_inbound, check_booking_link, check_compliance, screen_sanctions, get_conversation · Private data: verify_business, check_quota, verify_company_record, mint_key · Public sink: send_message, capture_lead, send_transactional_confirmation, check_compliance, mint_key · Destructive: check_compliance

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
